# Pandamonium v1.0.33

Pandamonium now keeps a native MAD MCP Portal conversation on the exact resource the Portal returned. This closes the contextual Qdrant failure found in v1.0.32 without adding another catalog, API fallback, or downstream connector.

## MAD-842 — Integrations: make MAD MCP Portal tools native and unify connection identity

### Problem

The v1.0.32 live acceptance passed direct Discord and Qdrant reads but passed the required contextual Qdrant sequence only 9/10 times. The failed fresh GPT-OSS run listed collections through Portal, then lost the returned collection identity on the follow-up and asked for information Portal had already supplied. Compact result extraction also needed to preserve whether a collection or channel value was an ID or a display name.

### Implementation

Pandamonium now retains only bounded, typed resource references from successful native Portal relays. It reconstructs named or nounless singular follow-ups from the immediately active trusted exchange, prefers the exact resource argument used by a read, preserves ordered ID/name references for listing results, and refuses to fall through to stale context after an empty or failed relay. The recovered value is fixed beneath the request-scoped Portal proxy and removed from the model-visible schema. The acceptance harness now distinguishes a read-only allow audit from an approval prompt and records executed rounds from tool evidence.

### Product value and UI visibility

Users can list Portal-managed resources and naturally ask about “that collection” or “that channel” without repeating an internal identifier. The existing single MAD MCP Portal integration card remains the only user/model-visible execution identity; its internal API companion stays grouped beneath it.

### Verification

The focused Portal routing, context, manager, acceptance, and release-workflow checks pass 55 tests. The complete local suite passes 5,560 tests with 5 intentional skips. Python compilation, YAML parsing, and diff hygiene pass; the protected PR runs the full Python, Chromium, syntax, secret, workflow-security, dependency, Compose, and container gates.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency, environment variable, database migration, provider credential, or downstream connection changes. The behavior activates only after the native Portal route is selected and only from successful internal relay evidence in the active exchange. Portal ticket TKT-000451 still tracks producer-side ranking of the original negation-heavy Qdrant prompt. CT103 installation and live GPT-OSS acceptance remain operator-controlled and are not claimed here.
